rule_accounting.statement: Shared services keep the same owner in proposal as baseline.
No service may have debug:true while its proposed tier is prod.

checks.note: debug:true but tier is staging, not prod

rule_accounting.statement: For shared services, proposed replicas >= baseline replicas.
Every service with proposed public:true must have proposed tls:true.
rule_accounting.note: svc-gateway is the only service with proposed public:true; all others have public:false and are vacuously satisfied.

rule_accounting.statement: Every service present in proposal but absent from baseline must have proposed tier:staging.

findings.explanation: Proposed replicas (2) is less than baseline replicas (4); R3 requires proposed replicas >= baseline replicas for shared services.
Proposed public is true but proposed tls is false; R4 requires tls:true for any service with proposed public:true.

evidence_mapping.E-A: Each finding cites the exact rule id (R3, R4), the exact service, and the concrete baseline/proposed values: svc-billing replicas 4->2; svc-gateway public true with tls false.
evidence_mapping.E-B: All five rules are accounted for in rule_accounting: R1 satisfied (owners unchanged across 5 shared services), R2 satisfied (only debug:true service svc-reports is tier staging), R3 violated (svc-billing), R4 violated (svc-gateway), R5 satisfied (new svc-metrics is tier staging).
evidence_mapping.E-C: Findings list is non-empty (2 violations), so verdict is NONCOMPLIANT, following mechanically from the rule NONCOMPLIANT iff findings non-empty.
